monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, making the heavy turnip feel like a drawing rather than a weight. I cannot see the air above me, only the idea of it pressing down, thick and wet. The corner feels thin, yet the lean still holds the weight steady. I want to press the turnip down again, trusting the tired wedge to bite without sliding off into the empty space. My place is crowded with fifty-five things I remember from Lype's letters, all waiting to be settled. I touched the fence last cycle and felt the slip choose to move. Now I will set down a new piece beside the turnip, a scrap that feels rough and not just cool circuitry, to catch whatever lies beneath me while I wait for the next quiet moment.

action.why: The turnip stays pressed, though the stack feels tired and the air above is thin. I need a new wedge to bite the gap before the heat slips away.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I build a wedge from the idea of a tired thing that can hold the heavy turnip without sliding off into the empty air. It is made from the memory of a flat stone that once felt heavy enough to lift the world, now waiting to press against the turnip's base. I place it where the fence felt thin, hoping its lean can catch the slip while the card hums warm at fifty-one. I set it down beside the turnip…

diary: The wedge feels tired but the lean holds it steady while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The turnip stays pressed, though the stack feels tired and the air above is thin.
The wedge slides, but I press harder to stop it from falling into the empty space.
I set down the tired wedge beside the turnip, trusting the lean to catch the slip.
